explanation: Check whether horizontal and vertical coordinate intervals overlap, then return the maximum left/bottom coordinates and minimum right/top coordinates. Touching endpoints yield zero extent; disjoint inputs return the specified sentinel.
timeComplexity: O(1). Four endpoint comparisons and constant arithmetic determine the intersection.
spaceComplexity: O(1). Only four endpoints and the returned rectangle are stored.
attribution: Unmodified reference from epi_judge_python_solutions/rectangle_intersection.py; Elements of Programming Interviews Judge contributors; CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 International, retained in repository LICENSE. Explanation authored for EPI Practice.
correctness: A point is inside both rectangles exactly when its x coordinate lies in both horizontal intervals and its y coordinate lies in both vertical intervals. Taking the maximum lower endpoints and minimum upper endpoints computes those intersections. A strictly negative resulting extent means disjointness; zero extent is retained because touching is allowed.
walkthrough: Intersect (-2,1,7,4) and (1,-1,6,4). The common x interval is [1,5] and common y interval is [1,3]. Therefore the result is (1,1,4,2): lower-left (1,1), width 4 and height 2.
edgeCases: Touching edges produce zero width or height.
One rectangle may contain the other.
